name: Jacques Roch
bio_short: Jacques Roch (1934–2015) was a French painter and illustrator whose brightly colored canvases are filled with comic-strip figures acting out small stories. Based in Williamsburg for decades, he showed at Holland Tunnel from its early Brooklyn years through posthumous exhibitions of his estate in Newburgh.
bio_long: Jacques Roch trained at the Beaux-Arts schools of Lyon and Paris. In France in the 1960s and 70s he made public mosaics, murals and painted sculpture for schools and civic buildings, and in 1971 the Paris publisher A. Balland issued a book of his drawings. His irreverent, often erotic cartoons appeared in the Paris magazines Pilote, Charlie Mensuel and Hara-Kiri. According to the gallery, he lived in Greece and then England, where Drian Galleries in London gave him a show in 1976, before settling in New York. By 1978–80 his comics were running in Playboy, Heavy Metal and The New York Times. In New York he showed at Exit Art, including the 1990 survey Ten Years of Painting in New York City, and from 1996 regularly at Kim Foster Gallery in Chelsea. He became a fixture of the Williamsburg scene, with shows at Side Show Gallery, 101 Grand and Holland Tunnel. Critics including Robert C. Morgan, Dominique Nahas, Denise Carvalho and Lilly Wei wrote about him, and he was reviewed in Art in America, ARTnews and Art Press. His paintings bring back the human figure as semi-abstract, cartoonish signs that pop out of fields of color. Holland Tunnel's Holland Tunnel Art Project published his cookbook Good Heavens! in 2001. He showed with the gallery in Brooklyn and on Paros, Greece, and after his death in 2015 his estate lent work to the Newburgh shows Esperanza (2018–19), the 25th anniversary exhibition (2022), Three of a Kind (2023) and Le Monde Fantastique de Jacques (2026).
practice: Brightly colored paintings in which cartoon-like, semi-abstract figures play out small stories against fields of color, rooted in his work as a satirical cartoonist and book illustrator. Earlier work in France also included mosaics, murals and painted sculpture.

verification.evidence: The Holland Tunnel site describes the same French painter (Paris underground drawings, cookbooks, Williamsburg, died 2015 at 80). Kim Foster Gallery's CV lists Holland Tunnel shows in Brooklyn and Paros and the cookbook Good Heavens! published by Holland Tunnel Art Project. Artnet gives 1934–2015, consistent with the gallery. Saatchi lists him as a Brooklyn-based French artist who trained at the Beaux-Arts schools of Lyon and Paris, with Holland Tunnel among his venues.

open_questions: The gallery says he moved from Paris to Greece in the sixties, but his CV shows French commissions and Paris magazine work through 1977 and a London show in 1976. Confirm the timeline with the estate.
The gallery mentions four cookbooks; only Good Heavens! (2001) is documented. Get the other titles from the estate.
The CV lists a 1990 'International Prints Show, Holland Tunnel, Paris traveled to Greece', which predates the gallery's 1997 founding. Clarify.
The Kim Foster CV spells the 1971 book 'Paris Ville Peige'; 'Piège' is assumed. Verify.
Birth year 1934 is from artnet only; confirm.
